subtype: Approach: separates a generation round from a selection round with agreed criteria [Revision]
passage: Sat in on Thursday's planning call for the onboarding project. The first twenty minutes went nowhere: each idea was picked apart the moment it was spoken, and Hansa, who had started to suggest a checklist, trailed off. Seema, the product manager, paused the call and told the group they would take ten minutes to throw out ideas with no comments at all. A timer went up on the screen. Fourteen ideas appeared. Then Seema wrote three headings: how much it costs, how long it takes, and whether users need it. The team scored each idea against them one by one. Four candidates survived, and Hansa's checklist was one of them. Seema plans to run the two rounds again next sprint, and I will sit in again.

qa.q: How many ideas appeared during the timed round?
What was Seema probably thinking when the call stalled?
qa.a: Seema probably felt concerned that ideas were being killed too early, which is why Seema paused the call and brought out the timer and the no-comments rule.

qa.q: What could a team try if loud voices still took over the ten-minute round?
qa.a: Everyone could write ideas silently on notes first and then share them, so quieter people get in before any discussion starts.

qa.q: How might Hansa have seen the two-round method?
qa.a: Hansa may have felt relieved and valued, since the checklist was heard and then survived the scoring.

grounding: Shows a product manager separating a no-criticism idea round from a scoring round using agreed criteria.
